prerequisites: Fundamental concepts of mechanics, especially static equilibrium
Basic statistical concepts: random variable, mean, variance
Basic concepts of elasticity and strength of materials: stress, strain, stress states produced by simple loads, shear and moment diagrams
Knowledge of ferrous material properties, especially regarding steel heat treatments
Harmonic oscillatory motion and calculation of natural vibration frequencies
Heat transfer (specific heat, overall heat transfer coefficient, etc.)
Kinematics and dynamics of planar mechanisms

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and capabilities for the calculation, design and testing of machines.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that imply knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
Students have developed those learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and evaluate the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.

assessment_rules: The final exam consists of two problems, each contributing 50% to the exam grade. A minimum score of 5 out of 10 on the exam is required to pass it. Passing the mandatory laboratory practicals is also a prerequisite to pass the course. Continuous Assessment Tests (PED/PEC) are voluntary and can improve the final grade by up to 10% only if the exam score is 5 or higher and practicals are passed. If the exam score is less than 5 or practicals are not passed (even with an exam score of 5 or higher), the final grade is a fail. If both the exam (>=5) and practicals are passed, the final grade (NF) is calculated as NF = (1 + CPED x CPV) x NEX, where NEX is the exam score, CPED (sum of PEC coefficients) is max 0.10, and CPV (virtual practicals coefficient) is between 0.8 and 1.2, with CPED x CPV not exceeding 0.10.
